summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of atrial fibrillation on Coumadin, dilated cardiomyopathy, systolic heart failure, diabetes, and morbid obesity was admitted for evaluation of bright red blood per rectum. He had recently lost 25 pounds due to increased diuretic therapy for heart failure. Initial workup revealed stable hemoglobin but a concerning colonic mass in the sigmoid colon. Colonoscopy and EGD showed high-grade dysplasia in the mass and gastritis, while CT scans showed no metastases. After multidisciplinary coordination and cardiac optimization, he underwent a laparoscopic sigmoid colectomy with lymph node excision. Postoperatively, he had brief episodes of hypotension and asymptomatic ventricular tachycardia, both managed conservatively. His anticoagulation was bridged with heparin, and cardiac medications were carefully resumed. He developed transient hypokalemia, which was corrected. He recovered well, tolerating a regular diet, ambulating independently, and passing stool. He was discharged home on postoperative day four with instructions to restart metolazone, monitor weight and INR, and follow up for pathology results and repeat colonoscopy in six months.
